source_text: Per quid igitur peccatum invenitur in parvulo? Per voluntatem? Nulla in eo fuit. Per nuptias? Sed hae pertinent ad opus parentum quos in hoc actu non peccasse praemiseras, sed, quantum ex consequentibus apparet, non hoc vere concesseras. Ipsae sunt igitur execrandae quae causam fecerunt malo? Sed illae solae opus indicant personarum. Parentes igitur qui conventu suo causam fecere peccato, iure damnabiles sunt. Ambigi ergo iam non potest, si tuam sequamur sententiam, coniuges aeterno supplicio mancipari, quorum labore actum est, ut ad dominatum exercendum in homines diabolus perveniret. Et ubi est, quod paulo ante hominem opus Dei dixeras? quia, si per originem malum in hominibus, per malum ius diaboli in homines, diabolum esse dicis auctorem hominum, a quo est origo nascentium; si autem credis a Deo hominem fieri et esse coniuges innocentes. Vide quamstare non possit trahi ex his originale peccatum
pass_a_gloss: Through what therefore is sin found in the little one? Through the will? There was none in him. Through marriages? But these belong to the work of the parents whom you had sent ahead as not having sinned in this act — but, as much as appears from what follows, you had not truly granted this. Are they themselves therefore to be cursed, which made a cause for the evil? But they alone indicate the work of the persons. The parents therefore who by their coming-together made a cause for sin are rightly damnable. It can no longer be doubted, if we follow your sentence, that spouses are handed over to eternal punishment, by whose labor it was brought about that the devil came through to exercising lordship over human beings. And where is that which a little before you had said, that the human being is God's work? because if through origin there is evil in human beings, through evil the devil's right over human beings, you say the devil is author of human beings, from whom is the origin of those being born; but if you believe the human being is made by God and that spouses are innocent, see how it cannot stand that original sin is drawn from these.

pass_b_english: Through what, then, is sin found in the infant? Through the will? The infant had none. Through marriage? But marriage belongs to the parents’ activity, and you had already said that they did not sin in this act—although, from what follows, it appears you had not really granted that. Are the marriages themselves therefore to be cursed because they caused the evil? Yet they indicate only the activity of the persons involved. The parents, then, who caused sin through their union, are rightly subject to condemnation.

If we follow your view, there can now be no doubt that married people are handed over to eternal punishment, since their activity brought about the devil’s rule over human beings. And where is the statement you made a little earlier, that the human being is God’s work? For if evil enters people through their origin, and the devil gains authority over people through that evil, you are calling the devil the maker of human beings, since from him comes the origin of those being born. But if you believe that God makes the human being and that married people are innocent, see how impossible it is to maintain that original sin is derived from them.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
